svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Cyclins control the cell cycle."], [1, "Different cyclins rise and fall at each stage. Cyclin D rises during G1..."], [4, "...cyclin E peaks as the cell enters S phase..."], [6.5, "...cyclin A rises through S and G2..."], [9, "...and cyclin B peaks at mitosis, then is suddenly destroyed."], [12, "CDK levels stay constant: a CDK is active only when bound to its cyclin."]]
svg.title: Cyclins and the cell cycle
svg.desc: A graph of cyclin D, E, A and B concentrations through G1, S, G2 and M phases of two cell cycles, with constant CDK levels, and cyclin binding activating a CDK.

g.data-info: G1 (growth), S (DNA replication), G2 (preparation) and M (mitosis and cytokinesis).
Rises in G1 in response to growth signals; with its CDK it drives the cell past the G1 checkpoint.
Peaks at the G1/S transition: starts DNA replication.
High during S and G2: DNA replication and preparing for mitosis.
Builds up through G2 and peaks at the start of mitosis; with CDK1 it starts mitosis. Destroyed at anaphase so the cell can finish dividing.
Cyclin-dependent kinases are present all the time but active only when bound to a cyclin; they phosphorylate target proteins.

g.text: → the cell passes a checkpoint into the next phase
